title: A Record Is Not the Thing
description: You carried nine sheets four days downriver. Minna Crale says the meeting does not read surveys. It reads field books, and the field books are in the Record Office.

the_field_books.title: The field books
the_field_books.objective: Go to the Record Office on House Street and ask Dorcas Fenn for the Rivermark field books.
the_field_books.journal: Minna Crale was polite about my survey, the way you are polite about a child's drawing of your house. The meeting reads from the field books, she says, and the field books are filed. Corse said it before I left: a record is not the thing recorded, and the field books still exist.

compared.title: Laid side by side
compared.journal: I laid the nine sheets beside the field books on Dorcas Fenn's table. They agree, line for line, in Pyke's hand and two others. My survey is a fair copy of something that was never missing. I am keeping it anyway, because a copy you are holding is still a thing somebody has to ask you for.

filed.title: Filed
filed.journal: I gave the survey to Dorcas Fenn and paid the penny a page to have it filed under my own name, beside the field books, as a record that somebody outside the house had held it. It cannot be unfiled. Anybody in Brackwater can now read sheet six for a penny, and the meeting knows it.
